title: Connectedness of a bridge of a subgraph
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, let $H$ be a subgraph of $G$, and let $e$ be an edge of $G$ that does not belong to $H$. Then the bridge of $H$ in $G$ containing $e$ — the subgraph induced by the $\sim$-equivalence class of $e$ — is connected: it has at least one vertex, and any two of its vertices are joined by a path within it.
hypotheses_covered: $e$ is an edge of $G$ not lying in $H$ (i.e. $e \in E(G) \setminus E(H)$)
